items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I did a couple of Woody Allen film soundtracks with Dick Hyman, he was the M.D.

ctx.x: So you get any studio work? I mean like commercial?

Sure — no, commercial, no, naah. I did a couple of Woody Allen film soundtracks with Dick Hyman, he was the M.D. And on one, I mean he needed acoustic rhythm and banjo, I mean he had like a full studio orchestra, that kind of rhythm playing. So I’m good at that. So I did that. And I subbed for Bucky playing rhythm on one track of that “Sweet and Lowdown.” But it’s not like — most of the jingles you hear or commercial music, it’s all rock oriented stuff, most of it. And I never got into that in the first place,…
when it wasn’t rock so no reason for them to call me now, that’s for sure. No, I mean I’ll probably do other like recordings for smaller jazz labels and those kinds of things.
